events.title: Ponce de León Sights Florida
events.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León saw the coast of North America and named the land La Florida. Tradition holds that he named it for the Easter season, the "Feast of Flowers".
events.significance: The voyage is traditionally regarded as the first documented European contact with what is now Florida. It began Spain's long presence in the region.

events.title: The U.S. Coinage Act Is Passed
events.description: Congress passed the Coinage Act, which created the United States Mint and set up a national currency based on the dollar.
events.significance: The act gave the young republic its own coins. It was a basic step in building a unified American monetary system.

events.title: Hans Christian Andersen Is Born
events.description: The Danish writer was born in Odense. He would go on to write some of the world's best-loved fairy tales.
events.significance: His stories, including The Little Mermaid and The Ugly Duckling, have been translated into well over a hundred languages. They are still adapted for stage and screen.

events.title: Union Forces Break the Siege of Petersburg
events.description: Union troops broke through the Confederate lines at Petersburg, Virginia. Confederate leaders were forced to abandon the city and the capital at Richmond.
events.significance: The breakthrough set off the final retreat of Robert E. Lee's army. Lee surrendered at Appomattox a week later.

events.title: Argentina Invades the Falkland Islands
events.description: Argentine forces landed on the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic.
events.significance: The invasion started the Falklands War. Britain won it in June 1982, and the war helped bring down Argentina's military government.
